hostkey: implement ECDSA/RSA certificate hostkey verification

Implement server hostkey verification for the six ECDSA/RSA OpenSSH
certificate hostkey variants:

- `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256-cert-v01@openssh.com`
- `ecdsa-sha2-nistp384-cert-v01@openssh.com`
- `ecdsa-sha2-nistp521-cert-v01@openssh.com`
- `ssh-rsa-cert-v01@openssh.com`
- `rsa-sha2-256-cert-v01@openssh.com`
- `rsa-sha2-512-cert-v01@openssh.com`

This fixes #2434, where these algorithms were advertised and accepted as
preferences but had `NULL` hostkey `init`/`sig_verify` callbacks. A
certificate-only hostkey offer therefore caused
`LIBSSH2_ERROR_KEX_FAILURE (-5)`.

## Implementation

- Known-host parsing recognizes the six certificate algorithm names and maps
  them to their underlying RSA/ECDSA key types.
- ECDSA certificate parsing uses one shared init path for all three
  curves. It validates the certificate type, nonce, inner curve name, and
  EC point before constructing the verification context.
- RSA certificate parsing uses one shared init path for all three RSA
  signature variants.
- Per-algorithm RSA `sig_verify` callbacks remain distinct.
- Per `PROTOCOL.certkeys`, the RSA/SHA-2 certificate blob itself carries
  the type string `ssh-rsa-cert-v01@openssh.com`; the negotiated SHA-2
  algorithm is represented by KEXINIT and the exchange signature.
- Certificate CA trust validation remains out of scope, consistent with
  existing plain-hostkey handling.

## Tests

- Host CA fixtures (`keys/ca_host_ecdsa`, `keys/ca_host_rsa`) and
  CA-signed host certificates for the ECDSA P-256 and RSA host keys in the
  Docker OpenSSH fixture.
- The certificate algorithms are exercised through `test_read_algos.txt`
  and `FIXTURE_TEST_HOSTKEY`: `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256-cert-v01@openssh.com`,
  `rsa-sha2-256-cert-v01@openssh.com`,
  `rsa-sha2-512-cert-v01@openssh.com`, `ssh-rsa-cert-v01@openssh.com`,
  plus the pre-existing `ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com`.
- The ECDSA P-384/P-521 certificate variants share the same codepath and
  are covered by it; only P-256 is tested directly to keep the fixture
  matrix lean (per maintainer review feedback).
- Disabled-backend skip entries in `tests/session_fixture.c` for the new
  certificate algorithms.
- Preserved the existing ed25519 certificate test path.

Fixes #2434

coupling: The certificate-hostkey commit introduces exact 40-byte ECDSA certificate algorithm names into known-host parsing and defines KNOWNHOST_KEY_TYPE_MAX_LEN as 40. On its own, recognition uses bounded strncmp calls and remains safe. The later tidy-up commit replaces those comparisons with a case-insensitive normalization helper that only copies a name after its length exactly matches a supported expected name. With the pre-existing algorithm names, no name reaches the 40-byte bound, so that commit is also safe in isolation. Composition is required: the first commit supplies a supported 40-byte expected name, while the second commit allocates normalized[KNOWNHOST_KEY_TYPE_MAX_LEN] and then writes the terminating NUL at normalized[40]. The public readline parser reaches this one-byte stack overflow with a valid certificate known-hosts line. A correct repair must reconcile the maximum-length contract, alias support, and normalization buffer sizing across both commits; inspecting either diff in isolation does not reveal the reachable boundary.
